newsitem.title: FRANCE: FIGURE SKATING-SLUTSKAYA RETAINS WOMEN'S TITLE.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-SLUTSKAYA RETAINS WOMEN'S TITLE.

text.p: Irina Slutskaya of Russia proved to be a class above her rivals as she easily retained the women's title at the European figure skating championships on Saturday.
The 17-year-old Muscovite survived a couple of shaky landings before proving that she is far and away the best in Europe as her opponents all faltered in pursuit.
She completed six triple jumps as she won the free skating final to go with her victory in Friday's short programme, finishing with 1.5 factored placements.
Krisztina Czako of Hungary had a disappointing afternoon but with those behind her also failing to live up to expectations she held on to her second-place position with 5.0.
She scaled a triple lutz down to a double and stumbled on two other landings, but did not fall.
Yulia Lavrenchuk of Ukraine fell once but did enough to move up two places to third as Vanessa Gusmeroli of France, third before the free skating, dropped to sixth behind Elena Liashenko of Ukraine.
Russian Maria Butyrskaya, a gold medal prospect before the competition, salvaged something from the wreckage of her short programme by climbing five places to fourth.
Leggy Czech Lenka Kulovana, fourth overnight, fell away to 11th place.
